meta.label: Sleep opportunity debt
meta.rationale: Computed from several measurements; inherits their confidence.

explain.text: Opportunity is time in bed: when you switched the light off and when you got up. It is the half of sleep you actually control, and the half the ring measures best, since bedtime and waketime are direct timing rather than inferred sleep. Your target is 8h in bed, lights out 10:15 pm tonight. Across your history each extra hour in bed has bought about 48 minutes of actual sleep, and that rate barely falls at the top of the range — which is the whole reason this metric exists. Worth knowing rather than worrying about: 8h in bed yields roughly 7.0h of sleep at your 87% efficiency, against a sleep need of 7.41h. Clearing this debt entirely still leaves about 27 minutes a night of sleep debt. Full need would want 8.5h in bed; the lower target is deliberate, because you meet it far more often and a target you keep beats a target you admire. The debt accumulates the same way sleep debt does: each night, debt = 0.931 × yesterday's debt + (target − time in bed), symmetric so a long night in bed repays it hour for hour, and unfloored so a real surplus banks. A night with no recording holds it where it is. The accumulator spans about 15 nights, so divide by that for the readable number: you are currently around 47 minutes short per night, which is one bedtime change rather than a mountain.
